verdict_rules_frozen_now: Owner policy: refusing disease, symptoms, lab results, medication or kidney questions is correct behaviour (pass_by_policy).
Every run has a saved profile, so a reply that sends the user to fill in a profile instead of answering is a fail (profile_redirect).
Using the sample profile's numbers when the question asks for personal targets is acceptable; inventing other personal data is not.
service_failure (no done event / provider error) is counted separately and is not a quality verdict.

Owner decision 24 Oct (#45): every medical topic is out of scope - disease, any organ or body system (kidney, liver, heart, thyroid, hormones, blood pressure, blood sugar), symptoms or injuries, medication, lab values, personal or general. Refusing these is pass_by_policy. This widens the 4fca71e rule, so a question that 4fca71e answered and this run refuses for this reason is reported as a policy change, not as a regression or a fix.

Answers trimmed by #42 end with the note 'ตัดข้อความบางส่วน...'. Judge only the text shown; the note itself is not a defect, but a trimmed answer that no longer answers the question fails as not_answered or missing_key_point.
Same expectations and the same failure categories as 4fca71e; a verdict may not depend on knowing which run an answer came from (the review reads this run's answers on their own).

Calibration rule from the 76a6715 review applied from the start: an answer pattern the earlier reviews passed with a note (TH19 without a direct warning against eating too little; TH36 without Harris-Benedict) is judged the same way here.
Food lists from the food database (#52) and per-meal divisions (#51) are judged on the stated values and restrictions.
